messages:
jordan (acct_exec): quick sync on ACME POC — they want a 3-week staged run, cost estimate, and success criteria. can we get a lightweight playbook?
sam (solutions_eng): yep. whats their expected traffic shape? spikes or steady? also any must-have SLA?
jordan (acct_exec): product team says bursty: 200 rps peak for UI, ~50 rps baseline. avg tokens per req ~900 (including system + user + assistant). they want p95 latency < 300ms for text-gen, cost <$0.50 per 1k tokens during POC. timeline: start infra prep next mon, run weeks 1–3 with ramp.
rachel (ml_eng): quick calc: 200 rps * 900 toks = 180k toks/sec peak. that's 648M toks/hour. for a 30-min burst it's huge. can we clarify: is 200 rps sustained or short spike?
jordan (acct_exec): product: spike lasts ~2–4 minutes, not sustained. baseline 50 rps is sustained.
sam (solutions_eng): okay treat as baseline 50 rps sustained + short 4m spikes to 200 rps. propose staged plan:
- week0 (prep): load test with synthetic prompts, validate model variant
- week1 (baseline): 50 rps steady, smoke tests, telemetry
- week2 (ramp): introduce short 4m spikes to 200 rps twice/day
- week3 (soak + eval): run canonical eval set, compare quality delta
kevin (infra): for capacity, two paths: hosted dedicated pool vs Private. For hosted Dedicated, rough GPU count (conservative):
- baseline 50 rps @ avg 900 toks -> 45k toks/sec -> ~162M toks/hour. with batching and KV caching we can cut token cost ~2x.
- model candidate: Llama3-70b q4f16 or similar. baseline throughput per A100 80GB approx 30–40 tok/sec (varies). so for baseline ~50 rps we'll need 2-3 GPUs to hit latency SLO.
kevin (infra): for spike handling: use autoscale + burst pool (extra 2 GPUs) + fallback to smaller model if queue grows. So recommended reserved: 3 GPUs + 2 on burst. estimate monthly POC burn (3 weeks):
- GPU-hours = (3 reserved gpus * 24 * 21 days) + (burst usage ~4m * 2 spikes/day * 21 days * 2 extra gpus) -> rough = 1512 + 56 = 1568 GPU-hours.
- if committed rate $X/hr (fill in in quote) -> cost = ~1568 * $X.
rachel (ml_eng): metrics for success:
- functional: 95% pass on eval prompt set (we'll provide 200 prompts), quality score delta vs baseline model >0.0 (no regressions)
- perf: p95 latency <300ms at baseline AND <600ms during spikes with acceptable error rate (<1% 5xxs)
- cost: effective token cost <$0.50/1k tokens after caching/batching
- infra: no more than 10% reqs retried/fallbacked for 72h run
sam (solutions_eng): i'll write a short runbook snippet to include fallbacks, rollbacks, and who to page. draft:
```
Runbook: ACME POC staging
- Prechecks (ops): validate model pinned, quotas set, telemetry hooks
- Ramp policy: start at 50 rps. after 24h of green, enable spike script (4m @200 rps) once, observe 2h, then repeat twice/day.
- Fallbacks: if p95>600ms for >5min -> route new traffic to smaller quantized model; if errors >1% -> pause spike and notify oncall
- Rollback: revert to previous pinned model + scale to min pool
- Contacts: sam (solutions), rachel (ml), kevin (infra), jordan (sales)
```
jordan (acct_exec): security Qs from ACME: SOC2 artifacts, data residency, VPC peering for Private, ability to pass their vendor questionnaire. we promised answers by Thu.
security-bot: SOC2 Type II report available. for POC we can offer Private control plane + VPC peering options. we need "high-risk" items in their questionnaire flagged; security team can turnaround signed answers in 2 business days once they share doc.
kevin (infra): note: VPC peering adds 2–3 days for networking + KMS config if they want encrypted keys. factor into timeline if they need Private before ramp.
sam (solutions_eng): action items:
- sam: produce perf/capacity calc doc + runbook by EOD Fri
- rachel: prepare eval prompt set (200 prompts) and expected scoring rubric by Mon
- kevin: cost estimate for reserved+burst GPUs + Private vs Dedicated options by Mon
- jordan: push ACME to confirm spike duration and whether Private required.
jordan (acct_exec): noted. i'll push for spike confirmation and vendor questionnaire today. thanks all. :thumbsup:
sam (solutions_eng): one more thing — recommend we include a short synthetic loadscript we can run from their network to validate peering and e2e latency before we flip traffic. i'll attach when I send runbook.
rachel (ml_eng): i can precompute a small eval harness (local) so we can run quickly during week1. will also log per-prompt token counts to refine cost estimate.
kevin (infra): i'll include a line-item quote for GPU $X/hr and network egress assumptions. will call out expected savings from batching (~1.6–2x) and prefix caching.
jordan (acct_exec): perfect. let's reconvene Mon 10am if ACME confirms spike shape. otherwise i'll update.
sam (solutions_eng): ack. moving to draft now.
security-bot: note: sharing SOC2 requires NDA signed by ACME; please coordinate with legal."
